headline: Hidden Third Form of Magnetism Discovered After 100 Years
meta_description: Three physicists win Europe's top physics prize for discovering altermagnetism, a revolutionary third form of magnetism that could transform computing and elec…
summary_short: Scientists have uncovered altermagnetism, a previously unknown form of magnetism hidden for over a century, earning them the 2026 Europhysics Prize.
body:
Three physicists have won one of Europe's most prestigious honors for uncovering a fundamental secret that physics textbooks had missed for more than 100 years. The discovery, called altermagnetism, represents an entirely new category of magnetism alongside the two forms—ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism—that scientists thought were the only possibilities. Professor Jairo Sinova of Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, Dr. Libor Šmejkal, and Professor Tomas Jungwirth received the 2026 Europhysics Prize from the European Physical Society for their breakthrough work. What makes altermagnetism extraordinary is that it combines properties previously thought impossible: like antiferromagnets, the magnetic moments cancel out and produce no overall magnetization, yet electrons behave as if the material were a ferromagnet. This unusual hybrid opens unexpected pathways for spintronic devices and future computing technologies.

The discovery emerged from eight years of collaboration centered at Mainz University, where Šmejkal first pursued doctoral research and later worked as a postdoctoral scientist in Sinova's group, while maintaining connections to Jungwirth's team in Prague. The researchers developed the theoretical framework by combining advanced mathematical approaches to symmetry with spintronics, the study of how electron spin can be harnessed in electronic devices. A major turning point came in 2022, when the team published a comprehensive classification of altermagnetism and identified hundreds of candidate materials. Experimental physicists worldwide quickly confirmed these predictions using spectroscopy and electrical transport measurements.

The significance ripples far beyond magnetism alone. Altermagnetism has revealed unexpected connections to topological phenomena, unconventional superconductivity, and other quantum materials. Within just a few years, hundreds of research papers have emerged, establishing this discovery as one of the most active frontiers in condensed matter physics across Europe, North America, and Asia.
quick_facts: Third form of magnetism hidden for over 100 years
2026 Europhysics Prize awarded to three physicists
Eight-year collaboration between Mainz and Prague research teams
Hundreds of potential materials identified in 2022
Could transform spintronic devices and future computing
